youtube.title: The Princesses Who Refused a God | Ramayana Ep 8
youtube.description:
A god offered them youth that never fades. A hundred princesses said no. 🌬️

On the road to Janaka's bow, Vishvamitra led Rama and Lakshmana north from Siddhashrama, toward a bow no king had been able to string. At sunset they camped on the bank of the Shona, and Rama asked what land this was. The sage answered with a story. King Kushanabha had a hundred daughters. Vayu, the wind god, saw them in a garden and said: be my wives, leave the human state, and never age. They laughed. We could topple you from your place, they said, but we guard our tapas. They would never slight their truthful father; whoever he gave them to would be their husband. Enraged, Vayu entered their limbs and bent them low. They came home weeping, and their father praised them: you have forgiven, as the forgiving do. In time he gave them to King Brahmadatta of Kampilya, and at the touch of his hand they stood straight, free of pain. Then the sage revealed that Kushanabha was his own grandfather, and that his elder sister had become a river.

📜 On screen (Valmiki Ramayana 1.33.8–9, vulgate):
"Kṣamā dānaṃ kṣamā satyaṃ kṣamā yajñāśca putrikāḥ, kṣamā yaśaḥ kṣamā dharmaḥ kṣamāyāṃ viṣṭhitaṃ jagat"
(Forgiveness is charity, forgiveness is truth, forgiveness is sacrifice, my daughters; forgiveness is glory, forgiveness is dharma. On forgiveness the world stands.)

instagram.caption:
The hundred princesses who refused the wind god Vayu

On the road to Janaka's bow, by the Shona river at sunset, Rama asked what land this was. Vishvamitra answered with the story of King Kushanabha's hundred daughters.
Vayu, the wind god, said: be my wives and never age. They laughed. We could topple you from your place, they said, but we guard our tapas; only our father, a man of truth, will choose our husbands.
Enraged, Vayu entered their bodies and bent them low. Yet their father praised their forgiveness: on forgiveness, he said, the world stands.
In time King Brahmadatta took their hands, and at his touch they stood straight.

📜 Valmiki Ramayana 1.33.8–9 (vulgate) · RAMAYANA — The Epic in Chalk | Ep 8
